ledger.claim: The recorded distances put this deviation at 1.60 km: 11.5 km actually driven against the 9.9 km recommended route, both figures from the platform's own trip record. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the two tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix - rows (c) and (e) - are unavailable and the rider is not shut out by the tolerance.

The route actually driven is on the record twice over. The trip record's rejoin event and actual_route_via show the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the KPE / Hougang Avenue 2 exit, running Hougang Avenue 2 and Airport Road, and rejoining at the PIE / KPE interchange; the driver-device GPS trace independently shows the same sequence of map-matched roads between 12:33:36 and 12:43:13. The trace is used only to show which route was taken and when, as POL-RD-22 directs.

The rider was never told. The platform chat log for this trip carries 0 messages and the trip record shows no in-app calls at all, and the record holds no call recording. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation; with an empty chat log and no recording, a verbal notice cannot be established and the deviation was not agreed.

The reroute was not traffic-justified on the very segment the driver left. The LTA traffic record for the KPE Hougang Avenue 2 exit to PIE, overlapping this trip's window, is of type NONE: no incident, roadwork or closure recorded, speed bands 5-6 throughout. POL-RD-23 admits only congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended route, so nothing in that advisory justifies leaving the KPE.

The one qualifying advisory in the record does not help the driver. It is an ACCIDENT on Upper Serangoon Road (towards City) near Kovan MRT - a road that appears nowhere on the recommended route as the platform recorded it (Rivervale Crescent, Sengkang East Road, KPE, PIE, Eunos Road 8). POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; this one is not placed on the recommended route by anything in the record, and a driver's bare assertion of an accident, with no such data on the route, does not justify the reroute.

The matrix therefore lands on row (d) - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - and row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full. On the recorded figures that fare is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, with no surge applied, exactly the excess_distance_fare_sgd the fare record derives. The rider is entitled to that 1.15 SGD back, and the present state shows it has not been paid: the fare of 15.40 SGD stands charged with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00.

The same money is owed on the alternative path, so the rider's case does not depend on how the traffic question is resolved. Even if the reroute were held traffic-justified, the driver did not inform the rider of it, and row (b) of the matrix - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km - refunds the excess distance fare. Row (a), the only no-refund row open at this deviation, requires that the rider was informed and agreed, and the empty chat log and empty call list put that beyond reach.

The rider's claim text asks for 3.00 SGD, and I do not overstate it: the policy's measure of this wrong is the excess distance fare only, and on this record that is 1.15 SGD, not the whole contested 3.00. The rider's win is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.15 SGD - part of the trip's charge returned - and that is the most the matrix provides for a deviation of this size. It is not a reason to withhold the 1.15: the charge is still live and the deviation is established, unexcused and unannounced.

No escalation is required to reach that result. The case fits a row of the matrix, so POL-GEN-26's escalation for an unestablishable fact is not engaged; the contested value is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence and no confidence floor or escalation is triggered on value; and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the 0.95 requirement does not arise. All eight artifacts in this case are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so nothing in the rider's case rests on impaired evidence.

The rider filed this dispute and the payments ledger records the metered fare of 15.40 SGD as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, so the present state is that the driver holds the full fare. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION outcome is party-relative and preserves exactly that state; nothing moves to the rider unless the POL-RD-24 matrix affirmatively requires it, and the rider bears the burden of showing that it does.

POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and on this record that fact is not settled. The advisory covering the recommended KPE segment, the very segment where the vehicle left the route (EV-ADVIS-06006-01), is type NONE; but a separate ACCIDENT advisory of an admissible 'incident' type (EV-ADVIS-06006-02) overlaps the trip window and the record itself leaves undetermined, for the judge, whether it lay on the recommended route. The driver's contemporaneous account that he avoided an incident is therefore neither affirmed nor negated by the traffic data, and POL-RD-23's required fact cannot be read off the file.

Because the traffic justification on which every row of the POL-RD-24 refund matrix turns cannot be established on this evidence, and because POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row to escalation, this dispute should go to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26; POL-RD-25 points the same way, since an AI ruling stands only at a confidence of 0.80 or more and the conflicting traffic data on the deciding question cannot support that confidence. An escalated fare is held rather than refunded, so the charge stands pending review.

Even if the judge were to move money to the rider, POL-RD-24 caps the excess distance fare at deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 = 1.15 SGD. The rider's claim for the whole 3.00 SGD therefore cannot be granted on any view of the matrix, and the most that could ever move is 1.15 SGD.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider's dispute is partly upheld. The recorded route distances show the driver travelled 11.5 km against a recommended 9.9 km — a deviation of 1.60 km — which is over the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so this is not a within-tolerance case. The driver did not inform the rider of the reroute: the trip's chat log carries 0 messages and there are no in-app calls or call recordings in the record, so under POL-RD-21 the deviation was not notified and not agreed. On traffic justification, POL-RD-23 admits only congestion, an incident or a closure shown by traffic data that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory covering the very KPE segment the driver left (EV-ADVIS-06006-01, Hougang Avenue 2 exit to PIE) is type NONE — no incident, roadwork or closure, speed bands 5-6 throughout. The only advisory of an admissible kind (EV-ADVIS-06006-02) is an ACCIDENT on Upper Serangoon Road near Kovan MRT, a road that appears nowhere on the recommended route (Rivervale Crescent, Sengkang East Road, KPE, PIE, Eunos Road 8), so it does not intersect the recommended route and does not justify this reroute. The driver's account that the KPE was jammed and an accident was shown is a bare assertion; POL-RD-23 says an assertion of traffic with no such data on the route does not justify the reroute. The POL-RD-24 matrix therefore lands on row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare in full. On the recorded figures that is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, without surge, exactly the excess_distance_fare_sgd the fare record derives. The rider asked for 3.00 SGD, but the policy's measure of this wrong is the excess distance fare only, so 1.15 SGD is returned and the balance of the claim is not granted. The driver's advocate argued the traffic question is unresolvable and the case should escalate; it is resolvable — the traffic data for the recommended route segment shows nothing — and the rider's alternative path (row (b), traffic-justified but uninformed) also yields the same 1.15 SGD, so the amount does not depend on that question. All artifacts relied on (trip record, chat log, fare breakdown and the two traffic advisories) are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; the contested value of 3.00 SGD is below the 10.00 SGD threshold at which POL-GEN-22 makes an AI ruling final; neither profile carries a fraud flag; and POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence floor is met, so no escalation is required. No referral arises on a route deviation in this policy version.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
